findings.evidence: Line 208 uses `hx.choose` in the map term; lines 269-274 recompute `hx₁`/`hx₂` and lines 275-288 use `hx₁.choose`/`hx₂.choose` with no note on why they match the map's choice.
findings.fix: Add a comment at the injective proof stating that `hx₁`/`hx₂` reproduce the same `exists_bar_eq` witnesses used to define `commFwdMap`, so `.choose` agrees; or factor the chosen decomposition into a shared private lemma/def that both `commFwdMap` and its injectivity consume, threading the witness explicitly instead of re-choosing.
findings.issue: `commFwdMap` builds its target from `hx.choose` (hx := exists_bar_eq h_fix p.2), and `commFwdMap_injective` independently re-derives `hx₁ := exists_bar_eq h_fix p₁.2` then uses `hx₁.choose`. Correctness depends on these two Classical.choose invocations producing the identical element — a syntactic/defeq coincidence with nothing documenting it. A future refactor of `commFwdMap` (e.g. deriving hx through a helper) would silently misalign the injectivity proof.

summary: Proofs are robust (group/simp/simpa/calc), free of show/change and undocumented defeq, with inline comments on the long blocks. One point: the injectivity proof re-derives the chosen decomposition via Classical.choose and silently relies on it matching the value baked into the map definition, which obscures why the argument lines up.
